🎨 What are Field Days?

Field Days are hands-on, screen-free days on the farm for kids and adults, ages 6+, running 10 AM to 2 PM. Every day is a different mix of skills and topics — from woodworking and fiber arts to plant walks, hikes, and farm salons. Come for a single day or make it a weekly rhythm: Register by Day or Register by Month. You can also read about recent Field Day and Field School projects in the Journal, or find out more about our philosophy and approach in the Policies and Resources section.

🪚 Woodworking
Learn basic woodworking techniques using simple hand tools.
💧 Working with Water
Water filters, rain catchment, pumps: cleaning and redirecting water to make it useful at home and on the farm.
🧶 Fiber Arts
Weaving, rope-making, and sewing — fiber into cordage and cloth.
🛠️ Sculpture & Fabrication
Clay, carving, molds, and making — shaping and fabricating by hand.
🌿 Plants & Animals
Studying plants and animal habitats in nature.
🎵 Music & Instrument Making
Music jams; learn to build and play simple instruments together.
🎨 Painting & Drawing
Drawing and painting sessions — we might even make our own easels and paper!
🔧 Build & Repair
Learn how to build and repair useful objects at home and on the farm.
🗺️ Maps & Hiking
Learn to use and make maps for navigation on local trails.

📅 Register by Day

Register for individual Field Days.

  • Time: 10 AM to 2 PM
  • Cost: $20 per participant (suggested; sliding scale at checkout)
  • No drop-off: adult caregivers must accompany children under 14 (but caregivers can attend for free!)
  • Safety, waivers, weather: you can find out more about these topics in the Policies section.

Register for a weekday, by the month — Field Days you can count on, to build community and work on longer-term projects together.

  • Time: 10 AM to 2 PM
  • Cost: $100 per weekday block — one weekday for the whole month (suggested; sliding scale at checkout)
  • No drop-off: adult caregivers must accompany children under 14 (but caregivers can attend for free!)
  • Safety, waivers, weather: you can find out more about these topics in the Policies section.

📋 Policies & Resources

A few things to know before you join us for a Field Day.

🌦️ Let’s Be Outside

Field Days are outdoor programs, and we’ll be outside in all but extreme conditions. We keep an eye on the forecast, choose sheltered spots when we can, and take breaks as needed — but the best thing you can do is come dressed for the weather. Layers, sturdy closed-toe shoes, rain gear, sun protection, and a water bottle go a long way. We’ll always let you know if a day calls for anything special.

🦺 Safety

Every Field Day follows established safety procedures, and our facilitators are trained in them. We review expectations with participants at the start of each day, keep group sizes manageable, and make sure the tools and activities are appropriate for the ages taking part. We don’t offer ‘drop off’ — children under 14 must be accompanied by an adult caregiver, who shares responsibility for their child’s safety and participation.

✍️ Waivers

All participants (or a parent/guardian, for minors) complete a waiver form before their first Field Day. We’ll share the form ahead of time so you can fill it out in advance and we can get started without paperwork on the day.

🗓️ Cancellations & Refunds

  • If we cancel — for extreme weather or any other reason on our end — you’ll receive credit toward another Field Day.
  • If you cancel — let us know at least 24 hours in advance and we’ll refund your registration for that day.

Questions about any of this? Email us — we’re happy to talk it through.

ℹ️ About

Waterbear Field School is hands-on, screen-free learning and building for kids and adults, on farms in the Lincoln, MA area. Ways to take part:

🎨 Field DaysA different mix of skills and topics each day. 📅 Register by DayDrop in for a single Field Day. 🗓️ Register by MonthA weekly rhythm — a whole month at a time. 📓 JournalRecent Field Days and ongoing projects. 📋 Policies and ResourcesWeather, safety, waivers, and cancellations.

Waterbear Field School operates as a recreational and enrichment program, not a licensed school or daycare. We don’t offer ‘drop off’ — children under 14 must be accompanied by an adult caregiver.
